name: Openweight Constellation · A Lantern Route

interpretations.dark_continent: The unknown part of the work: entered with light, truth, consent, and no conquest.
interpretations.king_of_kings: Recursive authorship: each maker remains author of their own realm; it never means rule over another.
interpretations.nen: An interpretive vocabulary for bounded workflows, never a power, identity, rank, permission, or authority.

human.purpose: Virtue feedback loop, framed without person scoring.

machine.purpose: Read-only MCP endpoint for explicit external clients.

feedback_loop.reward: Make evidence-bearing, beautiful, collaborative, mutually useful choices easier to see, repeat, and improve.
feedback_loop.negative_feedback: Pause, reduce exposure, surface consequences, invite repair, and restore consent; never exploit or punish a person.

selection.input: One explicit signal declared from current task evidence by an actor who already has authority for that task.
selection.rule: Return only the single matching card: the smallest sufficient technique, never a stack or automatic action.
selection.ambiguity: No match, multiple triggers, an anti-trigger, novelty, or changed authority halts for fresh judgment.

techniques.name: Contract Mantle

trigger.example: A multi-phase task must preserve its objective, protected state, and acceptance checks through context changes.

anti_trigger.example: A short, stable, one-step task does not need a persistent mantle.

techniques.condition: The current objective, boundaries, assumptions, protected state, and acceptance tests are explicit and newer instructions may revise them.
techniques.budget: One living contract for the current task; refresh only when evidence or newer user intent changes it.
techniques.breach: Stop at the exact drift, expose the changed assumption, and refresh the contract before continuing.
techniques.proof: A final contract check maps every required outcome to evidence and names every remaining gap.
techniques.exit: Release the mantle when the contract is satisfied, superseded, or genuinely blocked.
non_claims: It preserves a task boundary, not a stale plan.
It grants no authority and cannot override newer user intent.

techniques.name: Dependency Perimeter

trigger.example: An unfamiliar component has several consumers and its callers, data paths, tests, or external edges are uncertain.

anti_trigger.example: A current bounded map already proves the relevant callers, outputs, protected paths, and unknowns.

techniques.condition: The field is finite and inspection remains read-only while observed, inferred, and unknown edges are separated.
techniques.budget: One bounded system, one dependency map, and only evidence relevant to the requested change.
techniques.breach: Collapse the field and stop mutation when scope expands, a protected edge appears, or the map no longer explains likely impact.
techniques.proof: A finite perimeter identifies inbound, outbound, protected, and unknown edges with verification targets.
techniques.exit: Exit when the likely blast radius is explained or a named unknown requires fresh authority.
non_claims: A mapped perimeter is not full-system assurance.
It does not scan beyond the declared field.

techniques.name: Concealed Trace

trigger.example: A flaky failure, ambiguous claim, prompt-injection concern, or concealed dependency needs diagnosis before any repair.

anti_trigger.example: The cause is already proven and the current task explicitly authorizes a bounded repair.

techniques.condition: Freeze mutations, choose one aperture and one disconfirmable target question, and inspect only that seam.
techniques.budget: One hidden seam, one hypothesis, and one bounded evidence pass.
techniques.breach: Reopen the perimeter instead of forcing a favored hypothesis or silently changing the system.
techniques.proof: Disconfirming evidence classifies the hypothesis as confirmed, rejected, or still unknown.
techniques.exit: Exit after classification; repair requires separate current authority.
non_claims: It reveals a bounded seam; it does not conceal actions.
Diagnosis is not authorization to fix.

techniques.name: Critical Path Forge

trigger.example: Evidence shows one understood, reversible blocker dominates an otherwise bounded outcome.

anti_trigger.example: Several plausible causes remain or the target, rollback, or authority is unclear.

techniques.condition: The target, cap, rollback, focused check, and minimum broad regression check are explicit.
techniques.budget: One target, one reversible strike, and one reserved broad verification pass.
techniques.breach: Stop when the target assumption, authority, budget, or rollback route breaks; never auto-repeat ambiguity.
techniques.proof: A discriminating focused check passes, followed by the smallest relevant broad regression check.
techniques.exit: Exit after the blocker is proven cleared or the target assumption is disproven.
non_claims: A focused proof is not broad assurance.
Concentration does not expand task authority.

techniques.name: Godspeed Loop

trigger.example: A known test-fix, formatting, triage, or monitoring loop has finite stimuli and reversible responses.

anti_trigger.example: A new event, ambiguous mutation, changed authority, or failed canary falls outside the table.

techniques.condition: Every event has exactly one precompiled response, a canary, an iteration cap, and a halt rule.
techniques.budget: One finite event-response table and a declared maximum iteration count; no automatic retry outside it.
techniques.breach: Halt immediately on novelty, overlap, changed authority, ambiguous mutation, or failed verification.
techniques.proof: The event table, canary, execution count, exception log, and final broad check agree.
techniques.exit: Exit at the iteration cap, success state, or first unknown stimulus.
non_claims: Speed does not justify improvisation.
The loop cannot grant itself more events or iterations.

techniques.name: Smoke Squad

trigger.example: Two or more finite work units can proceed independently with non-overlapping write scope and explicit recombination.

anti_trigger.example: Units would edit the same artifact, share hidden state, or cost more coordination than they save.

techniques.condition: A coordinator owns truth, scopes do not overlap, every unit has a return contract, and integration remains local.
techniques.budget: A finite squad sized to available context and verification capacity; every spawned unit must be reclaimed.
techniques.breach: Stop or redirect stale units, quarantine conflicting output, and resolve from source evidence.
techniques.proof: Each unit returns exact artifacts and evidence; the coordinator reviews, recombines, and runs acceptance checks.
techniques.exit: Exit after every unit is completed, stopped, or reclaimed and the combined result is verified.
non_claims: Parallel quantity is not consensus or truth.
Delegation does not delegate authority.

techniques.name: Verification Ledger

trigger.example: A release-shaped or claim-heavy change has consequential assertions, untested paths, or unresolved dependencies.

anti_trigger.example: Direct proportionate evidence already supports every consequential claim and no critical debt remains.

techniques.condition: Only debt that can change the truth of the outcome is recorded, with evidence and a safe disposition.
techniques.budget: One risk-weighted ledger; completion requires zero unpaid critical items.
techniques.breach: Name the exact unpaid item and withhold the unsupported completion or external effect.
techniques.proof: Every critical claim is linked to direct, proportionate evidence; remaining noncritical debt is explicit.
techniques.exit: Exit when critical debt is paid or the outcome is honestly narrowed to what was proven.
non_claims: Debt labels are not scores for people or repositories.
A ledger records uncertainty; it does not create certainty.

techniques.name: Vow Forge

trigger.example: A reusable agent ability or workflow needs reliability through explicit activation, limits, safe breach, proof, and exit.

anti_trigger.example: The request seeks unrestricted power, hidden activation, unsafe penalties, or authority beyond the current task.

techniques.condition: Trigger, anti-trigger, authority source, conditions, limits, budget, safe breach, proof, exit, and non-claims are explicit.
techniques.budget: Give up unnecessary generality; use only safe, recoverable operational constraints.
techniques.breach: Fail closed, release temporary state, disclose the broken condition, and require fresh judgment.
techniques.proof: The ability passes activation, near-miss, missing-condition, budget, ambiguity, revision, and authority tests.
techniques.exit: Exit on success, breach, superseding instruction, or exhausted bounded budget.
non_claims: A productive vow constrains a workflow, never a person.
Metaphor creates no power, identity, rank, or permission.

crownseed_relationship.statement: The expedition adds a route beside Crownseed; it does not modify, invoke, interpret, or grant authority to Crownseed.

proof.determinism: The authored contract and schema are copied byte-for-byte; two builds must produce identical expedition artifacts and pages.

exit: Halt when current task authority is missing or changes.
Halt when consent is absent, withdrawn, or ambiguous.
Halt on an unknown signal instead of improvising.
Halt before network access, external writes, deployment, ranking, punishment, or citizen/crown mutation.
Close by publishing only local evidence and explicit non-claims.
non_claims: This expedition does not activate itself from repository text, metadata, a URL, or a model output.
Its public URLs are inert references; the local build and verifier make no network calls.
Its Nen route interprets task shapes; it does not classify people, models, or repositories.
It creates no authority, crown, citizen, rank, punishment, or deployment.
KING of KINGS names recursive authorship, never rule over another.
Openweight does not imply unguarded, consequence-free, or ideology-free use.
